objective: Close two gaps docs/STEP-12B-BACKLOG.md recorded during the connected integration pass ("The proposal validator's unknown-field rule stops at the top level" and "`failProbe` still has no caller") and deferred only because an acceptance run was live. (1) `validateProposal` in server/services/russell/proposal.ts (~259) refuses a whole proposal for an unknown top-level field (KNOWN_FIELDS ~122, loop ~272) — the rule §24 states — but inside the `candidate` (~329-355), `probe` (~360-386) and `software` (~389-424) objects an unrecognised key is silently ignored, so §24's claim is broader than the code: a worker that believed an extra instruction nested in one of those objects would take effect has it dropped and the rest acted on. The turn manifest in server/services/russell/turn.ts already tells workers exactly `title`/`statement`/`duplicateOf` for a candidate (~420, ~500) and `title`/`objective`/`expectedOutcome` for software (~438), so compliant workers are unaffected. (2) `failProbe` (server/repos/russellProbes.ts ~293) has no caller: `runProbe` (server/services/russell/probe.ts ~169) catches network failures inside `fetchOnce`, but any other exception thrown after `startProbe` (for example a failed `permitLookup` or `recordObservation` write) escapes, leaves the probe RUNNING, and is resolved only when `listExpiredProbes` ends it at UNKNOWN on a later tick — so "the probe crashed" and "the probe ran out of time" are recorded identically and the candidate waits out the deadline.
expectedOutcome: proposal.ts exports the allowed key sets for each part (candidate: title, statement, duplicateOf; probe: question, maxLookups; software: title, objective, expectedOutcome) and `validateProposal` refuses the whole proposal with a new refusal code `UNKNOWN_PART_FIELD` (added to the refusal union) when any of those objects carries a key outside its set, before anything else about that part is used; the refusal sentence names the part but not the offending key's value. probe.ts wraps the body of `runProbe` after `startProbe` so that an exception calls `failProbe` with a fixed explanation naming the failure category (the error's class name, never its message, since a message can carry row values) and returns `{ ok: false, reason: 'failed', outcome: null, lookups }` instead of throwing; a probe already COMPLETE is not overwritten (failProbe is guarded on PENDING/RUNNING). A FAILED probe is already picked up by the post-probe re-judgement (`probedAwaitingDecision` in server/services/russell/loop.ts reads state IN ('COMPLETE','FAILED')), so no loop change is needed.
nonGoals: Changing the turn manifest in server/services/russell/turn.ts, the action set, REQUIRED_PART, FIELD_LIMITS or any refusal that exists today.
Stripping unknown keys instead of refusing: the rule is refusal of the whole proposal.
Changing the probe envelope, the lookup budget, the verdict rules, listExpiredProbes or the loop.
Recording an exception's message or stack in russell_probes.
Editing docs/STEP-12B-BACKLOG.md (it belongs to another objective's scope).
Any migration, schema or policy change.

acceptanceConditions.statement: validateProposal refuses with UNKNOWN_PART_FIELD a CAPTURE_CANDIDATE proposal whose candidate carries an extra key (e.g. "projectId" or "priority" nested inside it), a proposal whose probe carries an extra key, and a REQUEST_SOFTWARE_CHANGE proposal whose software carries "repository"; each otherwise-identical proposal without the extra key validates exactly as before.

Every key in each exported part key set appears as a quoted field name in server/services/russell/turn.ts's manifest instructions for the parts the manifest describes (candidate and software), asserted by reading that file, so the validator cannot refuse a key workers are told to send.

When a step inside runProbe after startProbe throws (the test forces this by making the observation write reject), the probe row ends FAILED with completed_at set and an explanation that names the error class and does not contain the thrown message, and runProbe resolves rather than rejects.
A probe that ran to completion is still COMPLETE with its verdict after the change, and calling runProbe again on a FAILED probe does not change it.
tests/russellNervousSystem.test.ts, tests/russellRecovery.test.ts, tests/russellSoftwareJourney.test.ts and tests/intakeToResult.test.ts still pass and the repository typechecks.

rollbackRequirement: Discard the branch. A stricter validator refusal for nested unknown keys and a recorded failure path for a probe; no schema, route or policy change.
